catalog_quote: [p. 219, §8.1.1:] 北部土家语有四个声调，故双音节的连调模式存在16种可能性。 [p. 228, §8.1.4:] 在图上，我们看到，在收尾音节的位置上，高降调53、次高平调44、低升调24和低降调21的差异消失了，都变成了一个平调。我们说，在收尾音节的位置上，土家语的声调达到了一个混沌的状态。我们将这种混沌状态称为声调的中和状态。 §8.1.5 声调中和状态不是轻声 声调的这种中和状态和一般的轻声（如普通话的）有性质的不同，主要有以下几点：1. 轻声指音节的音强比正常音节弱，音长比正常音节短，音色比正常音节更为含混。在听感上，土家语双音词的收尾音节的音强不见得弱，音长不见得短。这是声调中和与轻声最根本的差异。 [...] 3. 如果说土家语有轻声的话，那么这个轻声不是出现在收尾音节，而是分布在起首音节或多音节词的中间的音节，类似于景颇语、独龙语等语言的弱化音节（戴庆厦：1984；戴庆厦、刘菊黄：1987；孙宏开：1991）。土家语的这种弱化音节不宜处理为轻声。 [fn. 79, p. 229:] 也许，土家语声调中和现象有与吴语上海话变调一致的地方：后一音节的调型变得不重要，整个双音节词的调型就是起首音节调型的扩展。参看许宝华、汤珍珠（1988）、徐云扬（1988）。

new_statements.translation: 1. A neutral tone (qingsheng) means a syllable whose intensity is weaker than a normal syllable, whose duration is shorter than a normal syllable, and whose timbre is more indistinct. Auditorily, the final syllable of a Tujia disyllabic word is not necessarily weaker in intensity, nor shorter in duration. This is the most fundamental difference between tonal neutralization and neutral tone. […] 3. If Tujia can be said to have a neutral tone at all, then that neutral tone does not appear on the final syllable but is distributed on the initial syllable or the middle syllables of polysyllabic words, similar to the weakened syllables of languages like Jingpo and Dulong (Dai 1984; Dai & Liu 1987; Sun 1991). These weakened syllables of Tujia should not be treated as neutral tone. [fn. 79:] Perhaps Tujia tonal neutralization has something in common with Wu (Shanghai) tone sandhi: the tone shape of the following syllable becomes unimportant, and the tone shape of the whole disyllabic word is an extension of the initial syllable's tone shape.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Northern Tujia is a four-tone language (53/44/24/21) with no stated word stress. In disyllabic words the final syllable's tone neutralizes to a level tone, but Zhang insists this is not a neutral-tone/weak-syllable phenomenon: the final syllable is not weaker or shorter than a normal syllable. If any syllables are weak, they are word-initial or medial (prefix-like), not final. Tonally the initial syllable dominates (the disyllable's contour is the initial syllable's tone extended over the word, Shanghai-like), while the final syllable keeps full intensity and duration — i.e. no consistent stress position is claimed; the source is silent on 重音.
new_statements.exceptions: Weakened syllables (弱化音节) may occur word-initially or in the middle of polysyllabic words (compared to Jingpo and Dulong), e.g. the a- prefix which can merge with the preceding syllable in fast speech (§9.1.2, p. 250); Zhang says these should not be treated as 轻声. Tone of a weakened syllable also lowers ('音节tsa53弱化时声调同时变低', p. 251).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain: disyllabic (and polysyllabic) words of the Northern dialect, based on citation forms and disyllabic sandhi data; the thesis never uses the term 重音/stress. The passage denies weakening (intensity, duration) of the word-final syllable and locates weakened syllables word-initially/medially; it is a statement about prominence only indirectly. Multi-syllable sandhi is explicitly left undescribed (p. 219).
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: Zhang Jun 2006 covers both Tujia dialects but ch. 8 (the chapter quoted) is explicitly restricted to the Northern dialect ('本章仅就北部方言的连读变调展开讨论', p. 219); his Northern data are from his own fieldwork at Duogu village, Pojiao township (坡脚乡多谷村), Longshan County, Hunan (thesis pp. 58-59), i.e. nort2732 proper. He gives Northern Tujia four tones 53/44/24/21 (the Wikipedia/other analyses give 55/53/35/21 or three tones at Dianfang). Other works listed (Li Jingzhong 2000 Luxi Tujiayu; ELAR deposit MDP0095 by Xu Shixuan) describe Southern Tujia (tjs), not this language.

Tujia 53/44/24/21), ch. 8 tonal neutralization: final syllable of a disyllable neutralizes to level 44/33; §8.1.5 (pp. 228-229) says this is not 轻声 because the final syllable is not weaker or shorter; weak(ened) syllables, if any, are word-initial or medial (like Jingpo/Dulong) and should not be treated as 轻声; fn. 79: the disyllable's tone shape is the extension of the initial syllable's tone. §9.1.2 (pp. 250-254) notes consonant/vowel weakening and syllable loss in connected speech ('音节tsa53弱化时声调同时变低').
